content.text:
droid-monkey attacked this Android app with a real-world fault and it failed. Fix the root cause.

## What happened
Attack `process_death` (process_death): Fill the screen's form, let Android kill the app in the background, then come back to it.
Steps: [{"fill": true}, {"fault": "kill_in_background"}, {"fault": "relaunch"}, {"settle": 6}]
Result: lost_state: 6 of 6 filled fields changed or emptied
Fields lost (before -> after): {'field_name': ['Ravi Kumar', ''], 'field_email': ['ravi@example.com', ''], 'field_phone': ['9876543210', ''], 'field_address': ['12 MG Road', ''], 'field_city': ['Bengaluru', ''], 'field_pincode': ['560001', '']}

## Diagnosis
Root cause: The six delivery fields are plain `mutableStateOf` properties on `CheckoutViewModel` (CheckoutViewModel.kt:14-19), and the ViewModel has no constructor parameter for `SavedStateHandle`. ViewModel state survives only configuration changes, not process death. When the app is killed in the background, the ViewModel is discarded, and on relaunch `CheckoutScreen`'s `viewModel()` call (CheckoutScreen.kt:34) builds a fresh instance with empty strings, so every field reads as blank (CheckoutScreen.kt:67-72). The screen has no other persisted copy of the input, so the user's entries are lost, which matches the six emptied fields in the verdict.
Fix approach: Make the form state survive process death by moving it into a SavedStateHandle. Change CheckoutViewModel to take a SavedStateHandle and back each field with `savedStateHandle.getStateFlow` or `saveable` state, keyed by field name, so values are written to the saved-state bundle. Keep `isComplete` and `placeOrder` unchanged, and keep the `viewModel()` call in CheckoutScreen, which injects SavedStateHandle by default. Optionally use rememberSaveable for the field values in the composable if the ViewModel should stay simple.
Evidence: app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt:13 - CheckoutViewModel is a plain ViewModel() with no SavedStateHandle constructor parameter.; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt:14-19 - all six fields (name, email, phone, address, city, pincode) are `mutableStateOf("")` with no saved-state backing, so they are lost when the process is killed.; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:34 - `vm: CheckoutViewModel = viewModel()` creates a fresh ViewModel on relaunch, so the form starts empty.; app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt:67-72 - the six CheckoutField calls bind directly to the ViewModel's in-memory properties, with no other persisted copy of the input.; verdict - 6 of 6 filled fields changed from the entered values to '' after kill_in_background and relaunch.

## Files to change
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutViewModel.kt
- app/src/main/java/com/shubhasai/monkeymart/ui/CheckoutScreen.kt

## Regression test
Add a JVM unit test `CheckoutViewModelTest` in src/test. It creates `CheckoutViewModel(SavedStateHandle())`, sets name, email, phone, address, city and pincode, then builds a second ViewModel from a SavedStateHandle that carries the first one's saved state (for example, `SavedStateHandle(savedState)` with the first handle's `savedStateProvider` contents). It asserts that all six fields and `isComplete` are preserved. Before the fix, the test fails to compile or the restored fields are blank. After the fix, it passes.

## Rules
- Fix the root cause in the files above with the idiomatic Android approach. Keep the change small and focused.
- Add exactly one regression test file under app/src/test (JVM unit test, preferred) or app/src/androidTest
  (instrumented), using only test libraries the project already has (see app/build.gradle.kts). It must fail on
  the old code and pass on the fixed code.
- Do not change build files or add dependencies. Do not touch unrelated code. Do not commit.
- Before you finish, call the compile tool on your test ('unit' or 'instrumented') and fix every error it reports.
- When done, reply with one short paragraph: what you changed and the test class name.

package com.shubhasai.monkeymart.ui

import androidx.lifecycle.SavedStateHandle
import org.junit.Assert.assertEquals
import org.junit.Assert.assertFalse
import org.junit.Assert.assertTrue
import org.junit.Test

class CheckoutViewModelTest {
    @Test
    fun formSurvivesProcessDeath() {
        val handle = SavedStateHandle()
        val first = CheckoutViewModel(handle)
        assertFalse(first.isComplete)
        first.name = "Ravi Kumar"
        first.email = "ravi@example.com"
        first.phone = "9876543210"
        first.address = "12 MG Road"
        first.city = "Bengaluru"
        first.pincode = "560001"

        val saved = handle.keys().associateWith { handle.get<Any?>(it) }
        val restored = CheckoutViewModel(SavedStateHandle(saved))

        assertEquals("Ravi Kumar", restored.name)
        assertEquals("ravi@example.com", restored.email)
        assertEquals("9876543210", restored.phone)
        assertEquals("12 MG Road", restored.address)
        assertEquals("Bengaluru", restored.city)
        assertEquals("560001", restored.pincode)
        assertTrue(restored.isComplete)
    }
}

content.text:
I moved the six checkout fields in `CheckoutViewModel` into a `SavedStateHandle`, so they now survive process death. The ViewModel takes the handle as a constructor parameter, and each field is backed by a small `savedField(key)` delegate that keeps the Compose state and writes every change to the handle. `CheckoutScreen`'s `viewModel()` call needed no change. `isComplete` and `placeOrder` are untouched.

I added `CheckoutViewModelTest` under `app/src/test`. It fills all six fields, rebuilds a second ViewModel from the first handle's saved values, and asserts the fields and `isComplete` are restored. The unit-test compile passes, but I haven't run the test or the process-death attack against the app.
